deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's 1983-84 notes on 'systèmes de pseudo-droites', i.e. arrangements of pseudolines in the projective plane. The previous pages work out sign distributions on faces of the cell decomposition X. This page computes a combinatorial monodromy (holonomy) for the 'polygonal structure' carried by faces strung along one pseudoline D_i.

Set-up (central figure). Along a line, faces F_0, F_1, ..., F_n, F_{n+1}, ..., F_{p-1}, F_p are glued successively, with p = 2n. The vertices s_0, s_1, ..., s_{n+1} lie on the line, and the edges a_{-1}, a_0, a_1, ... separate consecutive faces. The faces alternately meet the line at a vertex or along an edge. Each face F_k carries a cyclically ordered set P(F_k) (its vertices or flags), identified with Z/NZ by a bijection φ_k.

Passing from F_n to F_{n+1} across the common element s_{n+1} / a_n gives a map σ_n: Z/NZ → Z/NZ. It is required to:
- (a) respect the polygonal (cyclic) structure;
- (b) reverse orientation;
- (c) send φ_n^{-1}(s_{n+1}) to φ_{n+1}^{-1}(s_{n+1}).
Hence σ_n is a reflection of the dihedral group, σ_n(t) = l_n - t.

Composition. Composing reflections gives
ρ_{n+1} = σ_n⋯σ_0 : t ↦ l_n - l_{n-1} + ⋯ + (-1)^n l_0 + (-1)^{n+1} t,
which equals (-1)^n(χ_{n+1} - t) = (-1)^{n+1}(t - χ_{n+1}), with the alternating sum χ_{n+1} = l_0 - l_1 + ⋯ + (-1)^n l_n.
In general ρ_p(t) = (-1)^p (t - χ_p).

The constants l. For a vertex s of multiplicity ν_s (number of pseudolines through s), l_s = n - ν_s. For an edge a between vertices s and t, l_a = n - 1 - (ν_s - 1) - (ν_t - 1) = (n - ν_s) - (ν_t - 1). Hence l_s - l_a = ν_t - 1.

Result. For p = 2n (even, so the monodromy is orientation-preserving), the alternating sum telescopes into a sum over the vertices on D_i:
χ_{2n} = Σ_{s on D_i} (ν(s) - 1) = n - 1.
This is the number of other pseudolines met by D_i, counted with vertex multiplicities. So the monodromy of the face-polygon identifications around the pseudoline is the translation λ(t) = t - (n-1) in Z/NZ (plausibly N = 2n, the ends at infinity).

Purpose. This continues the program of the previous page: describe the combinatorial invariants (signs ε, cyclic labellings of faces) intrinsically from (X, K, S_K), 'sans avoir à utiliser les axes cartésiens'. Top-left sketches show oriented polygonal faces around a vertex on a disk.
errors: No substantive errors. The algebra for σ_n, the compositions and χ_{n+1} checks out, as does l_s - l_a = ν_t - 1.
The crossed-out NB formula (-1)^{p-1}(χ_p - t) is actually equivalent to (-1)^p(t - χ_p), so it was struck out unnecessarily.

The identification of N, and the exact pairing of l_s and l_a terms with the sign of the alternating sum, are left implicit. The pairing must be arranged so that each (l_s - l_a) pair contributes ν_t - 1; this depends on the indexing convention at the starting face F_0.

ideas.what: Gluing maps between cyclically labelled face polygons are reflections t ↦ l - t in the dihedral group of Z/NZ; the composite around a closed chain is a translation by an alternating sum
ideas.modern_name: combinatorial holonomy / monodromy of a dihedral (polygonal) structure on a cell complex
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (discrete holonomy computations); no specific attribution

ideas.what: The monodromy along a pseudoline equals Σ (ν(s)-1) over the vertices on it, which equals n-1 (the number of other lines crossed)
ideas.modern_name: local combinatorics of pseudoline arrangements (vertex multiplicities, zone of a pseudoline)

ideas.what: Encoding faces of an arrangement by cyclic labellings via Z/NZ, aiming at an intrinsic description without coordinate axes
ideas.modern_name: cyclic / allowable-sequence descriptions of arrangements; oriented matroid chirotopes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Goodman–Pollack (allowable sequences), Folkman–Lawrence (1978) / Bland–Las Vergnas (oriented matroids)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine dihedral-group computation (composition of reflections giving a translation) serving Grothendieck's private reconstruction of pseudoline-arrangement combinatorics. The final count n-1 is elementary, and nothing goes beyond what is known in the arrangement / oriented-matroid literature.
transcription_corrections: Under the sum: likely 's décrivant D_i' (s ranging over the vertices on D_i), annotated 'multiplicité des sommets', rather than 's dominant par D_i'.
Last line: should read σ_{p-1}σ_{p-2}⋯σ_0(t) = (-1)^{p-1}… (underbraced ρ_p), not σ_{p-1}σ_p⋯.
Top: the sum (ν_{s_1}-1)+(ν_{s_2}-1)+⋯+(ν_{s_n}-1) seems annotated with ν_{s_0} beneath as a side term.
Monodromy line: 'Monodromie des F_p : F_0 se fait par t ↦ … (translation)'. The crossed-out target is illegible; the underlined words beneath appear to describe it as a translation.
The 'l_n … 0' under item c) are the labels of φ_n^{-1}(s_{n+1}) = l_n and φ_{n+1}^{-1}(s_{n+1}) = 0, which justify σ_n(t) = l_n - t.
The reverse side shows a CRAY2 job listing dated 17 Aug 82 (scrap computer paper).
